findings.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — Backup-code consumption uses an unconditional read–modify–write, allowing concurrent logins to reuse the same code or restore each other’s consumed codes; consumption must use an atomic conditional update.

apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:135 — Successful 2FA activation defers onEnable() until the backup dialog’s Close button is clicked, so Escape or other dismissal controls skip the callback and leave the caller uninformed.

apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:281 — The copy handler reports success without awaiting navigator.clipboard.writeText() or handling rejection, falsely telling users their recovery codes were saved when clipboard access fails.

packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — tabIndex={-1} removes the password-visibility button from keyboard navigation across all PasswordField instances, preventing keyboard-only users from accessing it.

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:135 — Successful 2FA activation defers onEnable() until the backup dialog’s Close button is clicked, so Escape or other dismissal controls skip the callback and leave the caller uninformed.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, line 132-135 shows that when response.status === 200 in handleEnable, instead of calling onEnable() directly, it now calls setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes). The onEnable() is only called when the user clicks the 'Close' button (lines 264-271). However, the Dialog component has onOpenChange prop that could be triggered by Escape key or clicking outside, and there's no handler to ensure onEnable() is called in those cases. The resetState() function only resets password, errorMessage, and step - it doesn't call onEnable(). This means if a user dismisses the dialog via Escape after 2FA is successfully enabled but before clicking Close, the parent component won't be notified that 2FA was enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:281 — The copy handler reports success without awaiting navigator.clipboard.writeText() or handling rejection, falsely telling users their recovery codes were saved when clipboard access fails.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 281 in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx that navigator.clipboard.writeText() is called without await and showToast is called immediately after, regardless of whether the clipboard operation succeeded. The code is: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n")); showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success");`. This means if clipboard access fails (which can happen due to permissions or browser restrictions), the user still sees a success toast, which is misleading. This is a real bug in the newly added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — tabIndex={-1} removes the password-visibility button from keyboard navigation across all PasswordField instances, preventing keyboard-only users from accessing it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows tabIndex={-1} being added to the password visibility toggle button in PasswordField component. This removes the button from keyboard tab navigation, which is an accessibility issue. Keyboard-only users would not be able to tab to this button to toggle password visibility. This is a real defect introduced by this diff that affects accessibility.
